whatFailed: Navigating to the prefill address the help centre prints verbatim, /{user}/book?type=12345&duration=30&email=...&notes=..., renders the app's fully drawn ERROR 404 page instead of a booking form, so no textbox named "Email address" exists to carry the prefilled value.

docClaim.quote: An example URL with a few prefill fields is given below: `https://cal.com/johndoe/book?type=12345&duration=30&email=johndoe%40example.com&notes=Test+Notes` You can integrate the prefill-fields with your booking page URL in a similar way.
docClaim.section: pre-fill-fields-questions (lines 21-23 of the snapshot). Upstream source of the same text: calcom/help repo, bookings/prefill-fields.mdx line 20; duplicated in calcom/docs repo, pages/core-features/bookings/prefill-fields.mdoc lines 17-20.

observed: HTTP 404. transcript.txt and invocation.json record one console error 'Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found)' and visible page text 'ERROR 404 / This page does not exist. / Check for spelling mistakes or go back to the previous page. / POPULAR PAGES ...'. step-1.png shows that 404 page fully rendered (headline, Documentation and Blog cards, 'Or go back home'), not a skeleton, spinner or blank frame, and the step returned in 10.07 s. The page has no textbox elements at all. There is no /{user}/book route in the tested tree, so 'book' is parsed as the [type] segment, no event type of reference-host has that slug, and the route returns notFound.
impact: Anyone who copies the help centre's worked example gets a 404 instead of a prefilled booking form; the mechanism the article teaches is fine, only its address is dead. Sharper hazard: because 'book' is now just an event-type slug, a host who happens to own an event type slugged 'book' turns the documented URL into a silent wrong-page load rather than a 404, opening an unrelated event's booker with the prefill applied.

rootCause.explanation: The behaviour is correct and deliberate, so the 'root cause' here is the routing shape the doc is stale against, not a bug. The tested tree's only public booker routes are apps/web/app/(booking-page-wrapper)/[user]/page.tsx and .../[user]/[type]/page.tsx (plus their /embed variants and /d/[link]/[slug]); there is no [user]/book page and no rewrite or redirect for one (grep of apps/web/next.config.ts finds only /booking/:uid and /bookings rules; the '?!book' comments left in apps/web/pagesAndRewritePaths.ts:62-64 are dead leftovers of the old booker). So /reference-host/book resolves to the [user]/[type] route with user='reference-host' and slug='book'. getUserPageProps parses those params at line 214, finds the user at line 233, then calls EventRepository.getPublicEvent with eventSlug='book' at lines 245-253; nothing matches, so lines 255-259 return { notFound: true } and Next renders the 404 page. That is the documented-since-2023 replacement shape: the same prefill query parameters do work on /{user}/{type}, which the sibling scenario prefill-the-booking-form-from-the-address-bar.web.1 proves in this very run (steps 1-3 passed on /reference-host/prefill-all-fields?...&email=johndoe%40example.com, reading the Email address textbox back as johndoe@example.com; it only failed later at step 4 on how the Additional notes textarea exposes its value). The doc sentence, not the product, is what is wrong.

notes: Not edition-mismatch, and worth stating plainly because this target invites that reading: the deleting commit b364a85ed8 is an ancestor of both the tested cal.diy tree and public main, so the route was gone from Cal.com's own codebase three years before the fork. Cal.diy is missing nothing Cal.com has here; the help centre is simply describing a 2023-and-earlier product. Not environment either: systemic cause 2 does not apply, the screenshot shows a fully painted 404 rather than a skeleton, and the 404 is a deterministic server verdict, not a deadline artefact. Not test-defect: the scenario transcribed the doc's own example shape for shape (its own note records this as DELIBERATELY RED) and swapped only the host for the seeded one, which is the honest way to ask whether the printed address works. Two extra observations for whoever fixes the doc. First, the article contradicts a sibling page in the same corpus: calcom/docs legacy/pages/developer/pre-fill.mdx uses the correct modern shape, `cal.com/rick/quick-chat/?email=attendee@example.com&name=John`. Second, `type=12345` and `duration=30` in the example are inert on the current booker even after the path is corrected: they were the old booker's event-type id and duration parameters, so the fixed example should read something like `https://cal.com/johndoe/30min?email=johndoe%40example.com&notes=Test+Notes` rather than merely swapping `book` for the slug. Finally, note the collision hazard the upstream issue itself raised: with `book` now an ordinary slug, following the stale URL against a host who owns an event type named `book` produces a plausible wrong page instead of an honest 404.
